exactProposedMechanics.start: Stationary comfortable bilateral stance, unlocked knees, organized ribs/pelvis. One inspected fitting ball at chest with both palms/finger pads on rear-side surfaces, thumbs comfortably behind, fingers comfortably spread, wrists comfortable, elbows below shoulders; no forced hand shape or throat pressure.
exactProposedMechanics.preload: No deliberate dip/squat, step, jump, rotation, overhead action or loaded push-out.
exactProposedMechanics.THROW: After one early individual THROW permission, smoothly project forward from chest with two hands at retained easy intent near3/10. Retain planted feet and balanced finish; ball follows a natural forward arc to the inspected contained landing area. No downward slam target, distance quota, catch, partner or wall return.
exactProposedMechanics.HOLD: After one early individual HOLD cue, retain the same secure two-hand chest position and planted feet for3s, park on own fitting rack over5s, settle behind the line over3s. No forward fake throw, press or release; ball stays parked until future permission.
exactProposedMechanics.cue: Coach selects and records hold_first or throw_first prefix before delivery. Explain both meanings, but do not preannounce the next choice. Address one athlete, allow pickup, confirm readiness, say exactly THROW or HOLD once. No startle, rapid barrage, reaction deadline, color-only rule or speed score.
exactProposedMechanics.retrieval: After all actions stop, every released ball settles and every retained ball is parked, coach confirms all lanes/queues/paths clear. Only actual released-ball owners walk out, pick up, carry back and rack. No throw while anyone retrieves. HOLD/non-release athletes do not enter targets or perform duplicate set-downs.

signals.THROW: One owned forward chest projection to the unchanged contained lane.
signals.HOLD: Retain the ball at chest, keep both feet planted, then park on the own fitting rack without a release.

cueResponseContract.cue_delivery: Address the individual athlete, authorize only that athlete to pick up, confirm readiness, then say exactly THROW or HOLD once. The athlete knows both meanings but not the next choice. No rapid cue, startle, color-only rule or response-speed score.

HOLD.after_action: Ball remains parked. Athlete waits behind own line until the scheduled rear reset; no walk into a target lane and no second set-down.

cueResponseContract.false_release_rule: Immediately shut all lanes; cancel subsequent actions until safe. Count the cue if actually presented and every release including a premature one. Coach manages any uncontained ball; only released-ball owners retrieve after explicit all-clear when safe. No replacement cue or throw is owed.
cueResponseContract.withheld_on_THROW_rule: Record the actual cue and no release. Keep the ball secure, park under coach direction in the remaining action allowance or delay shutdown. This consumes the opportunity; do not issue another THROW.
cueResponseContract.all_clear: Before collection, every action has stopped, every released ball is settled and all held balls are securely parked. Coach confirms the entire retrieval area and queues are clear. No throw while anyone retrieves.

geometry.fitRule: Each assigned lane ball/rack must fit every athlete using it; no hidden zero-time swapping. Actual pace/fit/sightlines may delay or omit work. Dimensions do not guarantee containment or safety.

P1.perAthlete: 2s chest start +2s reach +2s return +4s relax =10s; palms comfortably forward/fingers upward, owned range, no ball or release.

P2.perAthlete: 5s floor pickup +5s chest hold +4s1m out/1m back carry (2s walking+2s turns) +6s original-floor set-down +4s exit =24s. Zero releases.
P2.entry: Comfortable standing/ordinary walking/turning and unloaded chest start. Coach selects plausible inspected ball and demonstrates. Unloaded floor access is known or observed in initial reach of SAME counted pickup before load; if unavailable, no lift, coach manages ball, partial observation recorded, no extra screen.

preparationContext.mainPlacement: Explicit active amendment retains40/140s preparation and assigns one known-cue rehearsal to E0 INSIDE the existing main opportunity total. No hidden preparation throw.
preparationContext.independence: A smaller P1/P2 branch neither grants nor revokes separately established main evidence; current handling/response still must fit. Quiet standing gives no arm/handling pass.

retainedStrengthContext.familiarTwoDBGate: Actual most recent compatible TWO-dumbbell record at the same pair/load/range/count with independently controlled pickup, top start, hinge repetitions and set-down, plus suitable current response. A single first OR06 loaded lesson or attendance does not establish familiarity. Actual OR07 unloading or a newer smaller record is not silently reversed; absent OR07 is not fictitious unloading history.

DB.setup: Five individually fitting elevated pickup/parking stations with TEN simultaneously suitable DBs at actual retained pairs/loads. One DB in each hand, palms facing inward, long arms and tall top stand with weights near thighs. Soft knees and organized trunk; move hips back with the DBs close through the actual owned hamstring-limited range. No floor-touch target or new range/handling test.
DB.sourceVsAuthorContext: Source331 verifies dumbbell-standard-tempo with TWO dumbbells on close independent paths and declared owned hamstring-limited range; related legacy RDL instructions explain hip-height start, soft knees, keeping load close and stopping before spinal compensation rather than reaching the floor. Palms-in/long-arm wording, fitting elevated pickup, handling clock and this small dose are explicitly declared OR08 session context, not a newly verified mandatory source profile.
DB.implementReuse: Push/pull precede hip today. Any suitable row implement reuse into later fitting DB pairs occurs only after row work is parked/cleared within declared setup; no hidden athlete carrying or incompatible pair substitution.

retainedStrengthContext.fallback: If actual pairs/stations/readiness/sightlines do not fit, deliberately choose a compatible unloaded set or defer BEFORE pickup. A post-pickup fault consumes partial work and ends the set; no replacement trial/set.

Incline push uses stable fitting support; row has opposite hand AND knee on bench, both-side accounting; fixed-arm heel tap needs tabletop/contact-return control.
